notes: Petitory action over land title/a purported lease to a gin company; dispute is about ownership and bad-faith possession, not compensated occupancy of a dwelling.

Negligence pleading case about a woman injured by a defective stable door while storing furniture; a tenant is mentioned but the holding is purely about pleading sufficiency, not lodging/letting doctrine.
Lease voided as let for prostitution outside the city's restricted vice district; concerns regulation of vice, not boarding/lodging-house letting or short-term room letting by a householder.
Community-property partition dispute over paving liens, attorney fees, and a wife's occupancy of the former marital home in lieu of alimony; not a compensated third-party letting arrangement.

holding_summary: In a succession partition, the court credited defendant, who lived in and helped support the family home, with the value of a dwelling she built there, financing it in part with her earnings as a laundress and from taking in boarders and lodgers; that credit fully offset her coheirs' claim for rental value of her occupancy.

quotes.text: she worked as a laundress, and had boarders and lodgers on the premises, for whom she did the cooking.
she worked as a laundress, and had boarders and lodgers on the premises, for whom she did the cooking.
We are therefore of the opinion that the claim for rents made by plaintiffs should be compensated in full by the value of this improvement.

notes: Boarding/lodging is incidental factual background (source of the defendant's income) rather than a litigated legal characterization, but the court treats a householder's taking in of paying boarders/lodgers as ordinary, legitimate income-generating activity.
Police-power case about a city ordering removal of railway bridge piers obstructing a street; no connection to residential letting or lodging houses.
Mandamus dispute over transfer of pledged corporate stock certificates; a cited precedent mentions rental value of stock, unrelated to real property letting.

Slander-of-title suit over a restrictive covenant requiring a 'single residence'; court holds the covenant merely personal, allowing construction of a triplex apartment house. Concerns real-obligation/covenant doctrine for multi-unit construction, not compensated short-term room/lodging letting or its regulation.

Upholds ordinance requiring movers to report household-goods relocations to police, under the police power; regulates furniture haulers for anti-theft/surveillance purposes, not lodging or boarding houses.
Boundary-line/servitude dispute between adjoining lot owners; no letting or lodging issue present.

holding_summary: A landlord who locked a tenant out of leased rooms and seized his belongings without resort to legal process, rather than proceeding by law to regain possession, is liable in damages for the illegal, self-help ejectment.

quotes.text: The plaintiff alleges that he leased two rooms and a kitchen at No. 1112 Frenchmen Street from the defendants for $8 a month and resided there with his wife and family for more than a year prior to March 4, 1922
A landlord has no right to obtain possession of leased premises by ejecting the tenants without resorting to the means provided by law.

notes: Ordinary letting of two rooms and a kitchen from a householder, treated by the court as a straightforward lease/tenancy and protected against the landlord's illegal self-help eviction.
Suit for the value of a horse illegally sold by a constable; a pleading/exception ruling with no connection to property letting.
Suit on a release bond after provisional seizure of farm livestock/crops for unpaid rent under an agricultural lease; not a dwelling/room-letting or lodging-house case.
Mandamus over a suspensive appeal in an ejectment suit concerning a farm tract lease; procedural landlord-tenant dispute unrelated to dwelling/room letting or lodging-house doctrine.
Mechanic's lien/prescription dispute between a materialman and a homeowner over unpaid construction materials; no letting or lodging issue.
Trespass suit against road contractors and a police jury for damaging enclosed farmland while hauling gravel; unrelated to residential letting.

Personal-injury suit by sub-tenants against their sub-lessor and the building's purported owner over a collapsed gallery railing; a sublease is mentioned incidentally, but the holding concerns repair-duty/negligence liability, not the character or legality of the letting itself.

Negligence suit over collapsed steps at a leased dwelling; turns entirely on proof of who owned/leased the premises (defendant company shown not to be lessor), not on the character of a lodging/letting arrangement.
